subject: crispr

resources.title: NCBI Gene
resources.notes: Reference database for gene identity, function and links to supporting records; database access alone does not establish learner readiness.

resources.title: ENCODE Project
resources.notes: Functional genomics evidence useful for target context and regulatory analysis.

resources.title: Ensembl
resources.notes: Genome annotation and comparative genomics reference; not a procedural laboratory protocol source.

resources.title: Human Genome Editing Governance
resources.notes: Governance, ethics and oversight reference for human genome editing.

resources.title: What Is CRISPR? - NIH STEM Teaching Resources
resources.provider: National Institute of General Medical Sciences / NIH
resources.notes: NIH educational material explicitly introduces CRISPR-Cas9 for secondary-school learners; used conservatively for foundation through intermediate coverage.

resources.title: Genome Editing Educational Resources
resources.provider: National Human Genome Research Institute / NIH
resources.notes: NHGRI educational collection introduces genome editing and CRISPR-Cas9 and links educator resources; it is not treated as advanced laboratory training.

resources.title: MIT 7.016 Introductory Biology - Recombinant DNA, Cloning, and Editing
resources.notes: Introductory molecular-genetics lecture covering cloning, PCR and genome editing; mapped conservatively to introductory CRISPR foundations and repair concepts.

resources.title: MIT 6.047 Computational Biology - Genome Engineering with CRISPR/Cas9 and Related Technologies
resources.notes: Verified MIT undergraduate computational-biology course includes a dedicated genome-engineering lecture on CRISPR/Cas9 and related technologies; mapping does not imply wet-lab proficiency.

resources.title: MIT 6.881 Computational Personal Genomics - Experimental Manipulations and CRISPR
resources.notes: Graduate course includes genome editing and CRISPR, experiment multiplexing, screening and selection, mini-labs, paper presentation and term project. It supports advanced conceptual/computational readiness but is not a substitute for supervised wet-lab training.

resources.title: MIT 7.15 Experimental Molecular Genetics - CRISPR/Cas Systems and CRISPR-Cas9 Screens
resources.notes: Course materials include CRISPR/Cas genome-engineering and CRISPR-Cas9 genetic-screen literature within an experimental molecular genetics curriculum; external readings require separate rights checks.

resources.title: The Basic Science of Genome Editing
resources.notes: Technical reference covering DNA break/repair, CRISPR-Cas9 development, guide RNA targeting, specificity and dCas9 regulation. The containing National Academies work is copyrighted, so this entry does not authorize local full-text copying.

resources.title: Basic Research Using Genome Editing
resources.notes: Covers NHEJ, HDR, programmable nucleases, CRISPR-Cas9 targeting, specificity and research applications; metadata/link treatment preserves copyright boundaries.

resources.title: CRISPR Technologies for In Vivo and Ex Vivo Gene Editing
resources.notes: Reference overview of guide RNA/Cas components, NHEJ/HDR editing outcomes, and in-vivo versus ex-vivo genome-editing contexts. It is cataloged as conceptual evidence, not as a procedural wet-lab protocol.

resources.title: Gene Editing and Genetic Medicine - Base Editing and Prime Editing
resources.provider: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
resources.notes: Broad overview distinguishes base editing from prime editing and explains delivery as a core genome-editor challenge. Used for conceptual coverage only, not procedural training.

resources.title: New CRISPR Genome Editing System Offers a Wide Range of Versatility in Human Cells
resources.provider: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
resources.notes: Authoritative institutional summary of the 2019 prime-editing work, including pegRNA-directed editing and reported specificity. Cataloged as research evidence rather than a laboratory protocol.

resources.title: Somatic Cell Genome Editing Program
resources.notes: NIH SCGE program documents development and assessment of genome editors, specificity, delivery to difficult tissues, and prime-editing advances. It supports research-level landscape coverage, not procedural competency.

resources.title: Targeted Genome Editor Delivery (TARGETED) Challenge
resources.notes: NIH describes current delivery limitations for CRISPR-Cas9, base editors and prime editors and independent validation goals for in-vivo delivery. Not a wet-lab instruction source.

known_gaps: Dedicated beginner instruction remains thin for guide RNA design, DNA repair pathways, delivery systems, off-target analysis, gene regulation, functional genomics, computational genomics, base editing and prime editing.
Base editing and prime editing are canonical taxonomy keys and now have explicit conceptual/research coverage, but neither is treated as beginner wet-lab instruction.
Delivery-system coverage remains reference-heavy rather than a complete instructional progression.
No cataloged source is treated as authorization for unsupervised wet-lab genome-editing procedures.

Research repositories, databases, program references and course modules do not by themselves establish expert readiness; expert status still requires practical validation, retrieval/citation checks and assessment evidence.
